subject.title: feat(linux): native gateway transport for Quick Chat — device identity, TLS pinning, ack-driven sends

question: Should Linux Quick Chat receive the local trusted-proxy password fallback for first-run pairing, matching the existing same-host Gateway contract?
rationale: This PR creates a native credential handoff and device-pairing path; source-level repair is straightforward, but maintainers must confirm that extending the established local bootstrap contract is the intended security boundary.

options.title: Preserve local bootstrap compatibility
options.body: Emit the password fallback for supported same-host trusted-proxy authentication, keep it out of the WebView, and cover fresh-install pairing plus remote rejection.

options.title: Deliberately exclude trusted-proxy bootstrap
options.body: Keep the narrower handoff only if maintainers document that fresh Linux clients must be paired through another approved path.

recommendation.title: Preserve local bootstrap compatibility
recommendation.body: Emit the password fallback for supported same-host trusted-proxy authentication, keep it out of the WebView, and cover fresh-install pairing plus remote rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the preceding Linux Quick Chat feature and authored the native Gateway transport and dashboard handoff.
